To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the network layers are not equally activated and that neurons can be mapped between robots with different number of joints.
(1) neuron activation can be mapped among robot networks, and (2) neuron activity of robot networks with small joint differences is mostly projected on higher layers.
neuron activation patterns in networks can be projected to networks with different complexity and that this projection accuracy increases with decreasing joint difference.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a better understanding of how the network architecture and neuron activation patterns of a robot manipulator with a specific joint number can be reused for other robot manipulators with more or less joints
the question how to analyze and reduce the size of end-to-end trained neural network representations of robot manipulators.
the question if the network architecture is a general feature extractor and a hierarchical organization for the task of reaching a goal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neuron activations in the networks trained for different robot tasks show a hierarchical structure that is reused in the different networks.
the network is able to learn general features that are used in the inner layers for all robot manipulator configurations.
the network structure is reused in a hierarchical manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
neuron activation can be mapped among robot networks with different complexity and the mapping is layer-wise dependent on joint complexity difference.
we find that the network trained for the 1 joint arm is the most general network and can be reused for the training of the other networks.
we can map neuron activity patterns between robot networks with similar joint number, but not between networks with different joint number.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we show that neuron activity can provide a means for a more detailed analysis of network structure in Reinforcement Learning and that neuron activity can serve as a feature extractor in the context of robot Reinforcement Learning.
we show that neuron activation can be mapped between networks of different complexity.
the network architecture and training process of end-to-end reinforcement learning neural networks can be analyzed to reveal the underlying feature extraction process.
